text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Newspaper headlines say Socialist leader Fatos Nano promised the return of investors' money lost in the pyramid schemes at a rally of thousands of people in Vlore.
- A newspaper commentary says the police are completely inefficient in front of the republic's guard which is controlled by President Sali Berisha.
- Statements from Alba multinational forces deny OSCE comments that they will guard the upcoming elections.
- People attacked, looted and burnt a military plant in Gramsh, southeast of Tirana.
- A 33-year-old British diplomat in Tirana, Jeff Briggs, was stabbed and later evacuated to Brindisi, Italy, for surgery.
- Prime Minister Bashkim Fino says he might ask parliament to be convened to review the distribution of proportional seats.
- The consumer price index in May was 1.04 percent higher than April.
- The newspaper editorial says Socialist leader Fatos Nano is using all his energy in promising to the Albanians in Vlore that their money lost in the pyramid schemes will be returned to them.
- Police arrest another young man in Durres concerning the grenade attack on President Sali Berisha.
- OSCE envoy to Albania Franz Vranitzky called on the country's political parties to sign a social pact.
- The Democratic party is trying to form an alliance with the right-wing Republican and the National Front parties.
- An Italian parliamentary committee will investigate some charges against the former ambassador in Tirana Paolo Foresti of arms smuggling.
- Vranitzky said the election coordinator for Albania will be nominated by the OSCE within the next week.
- After loosing much money in the failed pyramid investment schemes Albanians deposit their money in banks.
